answers.question: How long before I can run again? A friend wants me to race the Thanksgiving 10K in five weeks.
answers.answer:
Walk only for the first 7 to 10 days, then start jogging again when the quads let you climb stairs normally and the blister is closed. A sensible path looks like this:

| Days after race | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| 1 – 3 | Walk 20 – 30 min, nothing more |
| 4 – 7 | Walk 30 – 45 min, easy spin or swim if you like |
| 8 – 10 | First jog, 20 – 30 min, very easy, stop if anything pinches |
| 11 – 21 | Build back to 3 – 4 easy runs, no quality yet |

The Thanksgiving 10K is five weeks out, which is doable but tight. I would treat it as a hard training day, not a goal race: jog the first mile, settle into a comfortable tempo, and finish strong if the legs are there. A PR attempt that soon after a marathon tends to go badly and lingers. If you want to do it, say the word and I will shape the next three weeks around getting you to the line healthy.

new.analysis:
## What Sunday told us
You paced it beautifully through 20, then the quads cashed out, which is almost always a strength and long-run-volume story rather than a pacing one. Your front half averaged 8:32/mi and your back half 8:58/mi, so the fade was contained; you kept running when it hurt. That is a big step up from your first marathon and worth sitting with for a week before planning the next thing.

## Why this week is so light
Marathon damage is deepest in the first 7 to 10 days even when it does not feel that way, and running through it is where people pick up the niggles that cost them the next block. Walking keeps blood moving without loading the quads, and the blister needs clean skin before you lace up again. If by Saturday or Sunday the legs feel genuinely fresh and the toe is healed, a short shakeout jog is fine, but there is no prize for being first back.

## What I need from you
Tell me what you want to aim at next: another marathon, a spring half, the Thanksgiving 10K as a real goal, or just a few months of easy running to rebuild. That answer changes everything about the block that starts the week of Nov 2. For now, eat well, sleep more, and enjoy being a 3:50 marathoner.
